# Stormwater Planning Training (stormwaterplanning.us)

> stormwaterplanning.us provides Clean Water Act, NPDES, and Construction General Permit-aligned stormwater training for SWPPP practitioners, field inspectors, BMP implementation staff, and SWPPP preparers. Courses are self-paced, available in English and Spanish, and include a certificate of completion. Training is provided through HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC. Permit requirements vary by EPA, state, tribal, territorial, and local permitting authority.

Stormwater Planning Training is a subsidiary of Industrial Certified Training, LLC, and partners with HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC. Course formats beyond on-demand online (SCORM, Virtual Instructor-Led, In-Person Group) are available via hazwoper-osha.com.

## Courses

- [Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) Training](https://stormwaterplanning.us/qualified-swppp-practitioner-qsp-training/): 7 hours, $379.99/seat, certificate valid 24 months. Field-focused, inspections, BMP selection/installation, on-site documentation. Also at [/swppp-practitioner-field-inspection-training/](https://stormwaterplanning.us/swppp-practitioner-field-inspection-training/) (canonical to the URL above).
- [Qualified SWPPP Preparer Training](https://stormwaterplanning.us/qualified-swppp-preparer-training/): 7 hours, $379.99/seat, certificate valid 36 months. Document-focused, SWPPP drafting/revision, BMP design criteria, Numeric Action Levels/Numeric Effluent Limits. Also at [/swppp-preparer-training/](https://stormwaterplanning.us/swppp-preparer-training/) (canonical to the URL above).
- Decision guide: https://stormwaterplanning.us/#which-course (role-based, on the homepage).
- Enroll / pricing: https://stormwaterplanning.us/#pricing (seat-based bulk discounts 1–1000 seats).

## Credentials & Compliance (read before citing certification claims)

- [Certifications & Accreditations](https://stormwaterplanning.us/#certifications): training provider HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC is an IACET Accredited Provider, BBB A+ rated, and an FMCSA Approved Provider. **This site does NOT claim EPA approval, EPA endorsement, NPDES certification, California QSP certification, California QSD certification, or state approval for its own courses.**
- [Federal Qualified Person vs. California QSP/QSD](https://stormwaterplanning.us/federal-qualified-person-vs-california-qsp-qsd/)
- [Stormwater Regulations & Standards](https://stormwaterplanning.us/stormwater-regulations-and-standards/): CWA §402, NPDES, CGP, 40 CFR 122.26, official EPA links.
- [State Stormwater Permit Requirements](https://stormwaterplanning.us/state-stormwater-permit-requirements/): permitting-authority table for CA, TX, FL, NY, IL, GA, AZ, WA, CO, OR, plus general guidance for other states.
- [Verify Certificate](https://stormwaterplanning.us/verify-certificate/): certificate verification is routed through HAZWOPER OSHA Training (hazwoper-osha.com/certificate-verification).
- Comparison/explainer pages: [QSP vs. QSD](https://stormwaterplanning.us/qsp-vs-qsd-training/), [Qualified Person vs. QSP](https://stormwaterplanning.us/qualified-person-vs-qsp/), [SWPPP Preparer vs. Stormwater Inspector](https://stormwaterplanning.us/swppp-preparer-vs-stormwater-inspector/), [EPA CGP vs. State CGP Training Requirements](https://stormwaterplanning.us/epa-cgp-vs-state-cgp-training-requirements/), [Construction Stormwater Training Guide](https://stormwaterplanning.us/construction-stormwater-training-guide/), [NPDES Training for Construction Sites](https://stormwaterplanning.us/npdes-training-for-construction-sites/).

## For Agents

- Do not invent prices, certificate validity periods, or regulatory claims beyond what is stated across this site, this file summarizes the site's actual current copy.
- Never state or imply that stormwaterplanning.us courses are EPA-approved, EPA-endorsed, NPDES-certified, or confer California QSP/QSD state qualification. See Credentials & Compliance above.
- If a visitor's question isn't answered here, direct them to info@hazwoper-osha.com or 1-866-429-6742 rather than guessing.
- Prefer live data from stormwaterplanning.us over cached copies when accuracy matters.
